themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: The big spenders reported and did not slow down. Microsoft's Azure grew 48% and it guided $170 billion of capex for calendar 2027; Alphabet kept $195 to $205 billion for 2026 and said 2027 will rise significantly, while its cloud backlog reached $561 billion (CNBC, Reuters). Samsung's chip division earned 106.5 trillion won, said HBM is sold out for next year and raised chip capex 62% (CNBC, Reuters). Oracle rose 10.73% on Oct 28 after promising positive cash flow in the second half of fiscal 2028. Investors split on cash: Alphabet fell about 10% premarket on $9.1 billion of negative free cash flow.
themes.for_you: Suppliers still get paid, so the chip and memory map holds. MSFT is the swing to watch today (close over 533.42 on 31.7 million shares). GOOGL is Wait; no puts into the gap. NVDA is left out of both lists: demand is intact but a cash focus can cap AI chip multiples.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: Power demand from the AI build looks intact: Microsoft guided over $50 billion of capex next quarter and $170 billion for 2027, and Alphabet will spend more in 2027 than its $195 to $205 billion 2026 plan (CNBC, Reuters). Baker Hughes, which sells gas turbines for data centers, still fell 7.36% on Oct 28 after a Q3 beat because the Middle East war cut oilfield service demand (Seeking Alpha, Investing.com).
themes.for_you: No action. GEV is 'Accumulate on pullback' and was 895.08 on Oct 27, just under its 912.09 to 969.38 zone; it closed at 878.03 on Oct 28 (Massive). BKR's drop is about oil services, not data center demand.

themes.name: Critical materials and geopolitics
themes.what: Lynas lifted first quarter revenue 55% to A$310.1 million on record realised prices of A$102.1 per kg, with floor price contracts covering over half its sales, but flagged shutdowns at its Malaysia and Kalgoorlie plants (IndexBox, Oct 29). Lula's win keeps Brazil's push to refine its own rare earths; Brazil holds the second largest reserves, but Benchmark sees no domestic refining until 2030 (Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, Oct 28).
themes.for_you: No action. Record prices and price floors support the non China producers, but none of these names is in a buy zone. China's rare earth export ban delay still ends Jan 10, 2027.

themes.name: Defense, drones and reshoring
themes.what: Boeing sold off for a second day on 2.67 times normal volume (BA 167.14 on Oct 28, Massive) after pushing its 737 ramp into 2027. Its defense unit's operating profit rose to $492 million from $114 million, but a $252 million gain on the HRL Laboratories stake drove much of it, and the F/A-XX award is not yet in backlog (Air Data News, Oct 28).
themes.for_you: No action. BA is Avoid; heavy volume selling two days running says funds are still leaving. Do not sell puts on it.

themes.name: Fintech and Crypto Rails: Stablecoins, Tokenization, Exchanges
themes.what: ARK bought Robinhood in ARKK, ARKW and ARKF on Oct 28 while HOOD fell 3.31% to 91.43 after its Q3 miss (ARK email, Massive). Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 on Oct 29 after the Fed's hawkish hold (FXStreet), which keeps pressure on trading driven revenue at HOOD and COIN.
themes.for_you: HOOD is the only Setups put candidate, but it is Wait and below its 96.78 to 112.04 zone, so no put. ARK's buying is weaker evidence than an insider buy. HOOD is left out of both lists: fund buying and falling crypto prices pull opposite ways.

themes.name: GLP-1 and obesity
themes.what: Lilly's Q3 revenue rose 39% to $24.4 billion on Mounjaro and Zepbound, and it raised 2026 revenue guidance to $91 billion to $92 billion from $85 billion to $87 billion; the stock was up over 5% premarket (company release, Quartz, TradingKey). West Pharmaceutical, which makes the pen and vial components, beat and raised 2026 guidance to $3.41 billion to $3.42 billion of sales (RTTNews).
themes.for_you: LLY is 'Accumulate on pullback' and above its zone: no buy into the gap. WST's swing needs a close over 398.67 today on at least 838,900 shares; its Oct 28 close over the pivot came on only 1.41 times volume.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: BLCO jumped 15.78% to 20.40 on Oct 28 on 8.93 times its 50 day volume after its Q3 beat and raise, a heavy volume breakout above its 17.76 prior high (Massive). Boston Scientific fell another 5.84% that day after missing estimates (Investing.com). WST reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.66 against $2.20 expected and raised its outlook (StockStory, RTTNews).
themes.for_you: BLCO passed the volume test but closed 15% above the prior high and well above its 16.13 to 17.69 buy zone: do not chase; wait for a pullback that holds 17.76 to 18.14. WST is a swing check today, not a long term buy.

themes.name: Robotics, Automation and Physical AI
themes.what: ARK bought Teradyne in ARKK, ARKQ and ARKX on Oct 28, about 0.25% of each fund (ARK email). AGCO is running Agility Robotics humanoids at its Hesston, Kansas plant, and Schaeffler has humanoids building actuator parts for other humanoids in China (engineering.com, Oct 28).
themes.for_you: No action. TER has no buy zone verdict to act on; fund buying is weak evidence on its own. Factory humanoid pilots are still small.

themes.name: Space, Quantum and Cyber: Government Funded Frontier Tech
themes.what: Fortinet fell 25.7% premarket on Oct 29 after its Q3: results beat, but product growth of 37% missed the roughly 50% the market wanted and it cut its service revenue guide to $5.15 billion to $5.17 billion; BofA downgraded it to Neutral with a $140 target, and an unconfirmed breach report added pressure (Investing.com). Palo Alto, Zscaler and CrowdStrike fell in sympathy.
themes.for_you: No action. None of the cyber names is in a buy zone. Avoid selling puts into a 25% gap; wait for the dust to settle.

innovations.name: Agriculture and Food
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. AGCO's Q3 (Oct 29) sales fell 8.6% to $2.26 billion, with Latin America down 19.1% and Brazil tractor retail sales down 17% for nine months; it kept its 2026 outlook and targets $2 billion of PTx retrofit sales by 2029 from about $1 billion this year. About 29% of global urea trade normally passes Hormuz (S&P Global), which keeps the cost case for nitrogen-fixing biologicals alive. No stage moves: the PRRS pig still waits on Mexico and Japan, and Corteva reports Nov 11.
innovations.for_you: No action on AGCO or DE; neither has a buy zone verdict, and AGCO's sales are still falling. CF is 'Buy zone now' (119.92 on Oct 28, Massive) and benefits from tight nitrogen, but it reports Nov 4 after the close (company release), inside any new put window, so no put now. Mark Nov 11 for Corteva.

innovations.name: Healthcare
innovations.what: Lilly's Q3 revenue rose 39% to $24.4 billion, driven by Mounjaro and Zepbound, and it raised 2026 revenue guidance to $91 billion to $92 billion from $85 billion to $87 billion, its third raise this year (company release, Quartz). West Pharmaceutical, which supplies pen and vial components, also beat and raised.
innovations.for_you: LLY is 'Accumulate on pullback' above its zone: no buy into a 5% premarket gap. WST's swing needs a close over 398.67 today on at least 838,900 shares.

innovations.name: Technology
innovations.what: Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum, a maker of lasers for data center optics, with a deal possibly announced next week (Reuters, Oct 28). If it closes, a major chip designer would own a key laser supplier for optical links, including co-packaged optics. MRVL fell over 11% and LITE rose over 6% premarket Oct 29 (TradingKey). The stage does not change: this is a deal, not new revenue.
innovations.for_you: Both MRVL and LITE were 'Buy zone now' on Oct 27 closes. No buy or put in either until terms are public; a pending deal caps LITE's upside.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.what: Day three of the post election sell off: the Ibovespa fell 2.68% to 171,006.10 on Oct 28 while the dollar slipped 0.19% to R$5.34 (InfoMoney, UOL). US closes on Oct 28: EWZ 33.62 (down 1.98% on 2.08 times normal volume), NU 11.97 (down 3.47%), ITUB 7.40, BBD 2.73 (down 6.19%), PBR 22.03, MELI 1673.09 (Massive). AGCO reported Brazil tractor retail sales down 17% in the first nine months of 2026.
countries.for_you: No action. Heavy volume on a down day is distribution; NU is further under its 13.10 line. Wait for the Nov 3 to 4 rate decision.

countries.name: China
countries.what: The yuan rose to 6.6620 per dollar on Oct 29, a four year high, after the Fed's hold; it is up about 5% against the dollar this year and the midpoint was fixed at 6.7147 (Reuters via Economic Times).
countries.for_you: No action. Left out of both lists: a stronger yuan lifts Chinese buying power but hurts Chinese exporters. FXI closed at 32.46 on Oct 28 (Massive).

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: Brent settled up 1.3% at $115.32 on Oct 28, then fell 1.73% to $113.32 on Oct 29 after Vice President Vance reached out to Iran's Security Council chief and Qatar offered a new proposal; a senior Iranian official rejected it (CNBC, The National). Baker Hughes fell 7.36% on Oct 28 as the conflict cut oilfield service demand.
countries.for_you: XOM and CVX are open trades reporting Oct 30: take profits or tighten stops today. Producers are left out of both lists: diplomacy pulls oil down, the post Nov 3 risk pushes it up.

countries.name: India
countries.what: The Sensex rose 905.01 points to 74,151.04 and the Nifty 1.05% to 22,936.75 on Oct 29 after the Fed held, led by banks and consumer stocks (Deccan Herald); the rupee closed at 95.25 per dollar (Economic Times). Brent easing toward $113 helps an oil importer.
countries.for_you: No action. INDA closed at 46.79 on Oct 28 (Massive) and has no verdict; one strong day does not end a downtrend.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: The Nikkei rose 1.1% to 64,659.25 on Oct 29, a fourth straight gain, while Korea fell, as SoftBank and Kioxia rose (TradingKey). The dollar climbed back above 158 yen before the BOJ's Oct 30 decision, which FXStreet previews as a hawkish hold.
countries.for_you: No action. EWJ closed at 94.99 on Oct 28 (Massive). Watch the BOJ on Oct 30 for open swings.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: Samsung reported record Q3 operating profit of 107.44 trillion won, about in line, with chip profit of 106.5 trillion won; it said HBM is sold out for next year and chip capex rises 62%, but deferred new shareholder returns to January (CNBC, Reuters). Samsung fell 4.13%, SK hynix rose 2.22% and the KOSPI fell 1.24% to 5,937.66 (TradingKey).
countries.for_you: No action. Memory demand is confirmed by both makers; the stocks now trade on payouts. Do not chase EWY after a 5.37% day.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.what: The Taiex fell 667.25 points, or 1.42%, to 46,368.33 on Oct 29, breaking below its quarterly moving average, as UMC hit limit down after its earnings call and Alphabet's drop weighed on AI names (BigGo Finance).
countries.for_you: No action. EWT closed at 108.94 on Oct 28 (Massive), before this drop. Do not add Taiwan puts while the index sits under its quarterly average.
